claims.text: POL-NS-23 requires the driver, before cancelling for no-show, to have sent at least one in-app chat message AND to have placed at least one in-app call, both before trip_record.cancelled_at. The record shows the call limb only — a single in-app call at 11:14:20 that was not answered and rang 20 s (EV-TRIP-05065) — and no chat message from the driver at all: the chat log's one and only entry is the rider's own message at 11:06:00, and the platform's own derived contact_before_cancel block returns message_count 0, complete false and obligation_met false (EV-CHAT-05065). I rely on EV-CHAT-05065 as impaired evidence: TRUNCATED_LOG, weight_multiplier 0.6, 1 of 3 entries exported with nothing after 11:06:00. On the record as it stands the message limb of the contact obligation fails, and POL-NS-23 is express that the fee is then voided 'with no driver compensation' — so the driver cannot recover the 5.00 under POL-NS-22 even though he cancelled 380 s after arriving.

The driver's claim says he 'sent message and called', but the trip record's own event log shows what actually happened at that pickup: a platform push notification at 11:11:54 ('Your driver has arrived') and one in-app call at 11:14:20 that was not answered (EV-TRIP-05065). A system push is not an in-app chat message, and an unanswered call is not a message; POL-NS-23 requires both limbs, each before the cancellation, and nothing in this record supplies the message limb. The chat log I rely on for that is impaired — TRUNCATED_LOG, weight_multiplier 0.6 (EV-CHAT-05065).

If the judge reads the truncated chat export as leaving the message limb unproved rather than disproved, the rider still wins the money point: whether the driver messaged before cancelling is a fact POL-NS-23 needs, and the only evidence that would carry it is impaired — the export holds 1 entry against trip_record.chat_message_count of 3 and covers nothing after 11:06:00, so the arrival and the whole waiting window are absent (EV-CHAT-05065, weight_multiplier 0.6, TRUNCATED_LOG; EV-TRIP-05065). POL-GEN-26 names this very fact ('whether the driver messaged and called before cancelling') and requires escalation. ESCALATE is terminal, issues no monetary outcome and holds the amount, so the 5.00 already refunded to the rider is not restored to the driver and no fee is collected from the rider. POL-NS-26 expressly subjects even a final no-show ruling to POL-GEN-26.

I do not contest the wait, and I say so plainly: POL-NS-21's free wait runs 300 s from the driver's arrival, the record puts arrival at 11:11:50 and cancellation at 11:18:10 — 380 s — and the GPS trace corroborates the arrival, the nearest fix sitting 2.05 m from the pickup at 11:12:30 with 5.0 m reported accuracy, well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius (EV-GPS-05065; EV-TRIP-05065). That discharges POL-NS-21 and it does nothing for POL-NS-23, which is a separate and cumulative contact obligation the driver must also satisfy before he may cancel for no-show.

The filer here is the driver (dispute.filed_by = DRIVER) and the disputed 5.00 is already off the rider: the ledger records payment_status REFUNDED with refund_issued_sgd 5.00 against total_charged 5.00 (EV-FARE-05065), and the trip record records the fee_reversed event at 13:59:10 — 5.00 refunded to the rider and withheld from the driver (EV-TRIP-05065). What the driver seeks is restoration of that 5.00 to himself. POL-GEN-03 defines FULL_REFUND against the filing party, so on a driver's filing FULL_REFUND would run to the driver; it is not the rider's remedy and the rider does not ask for it. The rider's entitlement is that the disputed charge is not collected, which is exactly what the present state already achieves: NO_ACTION — the filing party's claim not supported, both amount fields null and no driver compensation.

No POL-NS-25 repeat-no-show referral is available on this profile. EV-RPROF-05065 carries no no_show_cancellations_30d counter at all, and POL-NS-25 applies only where that counter is present, so the flag cannot be computed and must not be manufactured from the record. The profile's no_show_disputes_30d is a different field, is CONTEXT ONLY under POL-GEN-01, and may not be used to qualify or decide this trip.

The driver's arrival at the pickup is established on clean evidence: the trip record's driver_arrived event at 11:11:50 is corroborated by the driver's GPS trace under POL-NS-21, whose nearest fix to the pickup point is 2.05 m away with a reported accuracy of 5 m — well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius — and the arrival check returns corroborated true.

The driver served the free wait in fact, not merely on paper: the driver's trace carries thirteen consecutive zero-speed fixes holding position at the pickup from 11:11:30 through 11:18:00, and the platform recorded wait_timer_expired at 11:16:55 with the rider not on board, so the 300 s POL-NS-21 requires was actually waited.

The cancellation came after the free wait: POL-NS-21's clock starts from the driver's arrival (11:11:50) so the 300 s free wait expired at 11:16:50, while the driver cancelled at 11:18:10 — 380 s after arrival — which satisfies POL-NS-22's precondition of a cancellation after the free wait.

The call limb of POL-NS-23 is satisfied on the clean record: the trip record's in_app_calls carries one call placed by the driver at 11:14:20, unanswered after ringing 20 s, which is before cancelled_at (11:18:10) and is exactly the trip_record.in_app_calls entry the clause names.

The message limb is not shown to be missing. The chat log is IMPAIRED — issue code TRUNCATED_LOG, weight multiplier 0.6 — because the export holds only 1 entry (11:06:00) while trip_record.chat_message_count is 3, and the absent entries cover the arrival and the entire waiting window. POL-NS-23 voids the fee only where the driver's message 'is missing', and the absence of a message from a truncated export does not establish that no message was ever sent.

The counterparty statement does not fill that gap: the rider concedes the call ('Only a missed call') and asserts only that he received no arrival message, and a party's recollection of what he did or did not receive cannot establish what the platform's own chat system carried before the cancellation.

With the arrival, the free wait and the call all carried by artifacts at weight 1.0, the fee is not voided and the ledger's own arithmetic compels the driver's outcome: the fare breakdown charges 5.00 SGD, the policy fee is 5.00 SGD, fee_matches_policy is true, so POL-NS-22 directs DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 5.00.

No confidence floor bars that ruling: the amount contested is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and the only profile field POL-GEN-22 makes relevant is fraud_flags, which is 0 on both profiles, so neither the 0.80 nor the 0.95 threshold applies, and POL-NS-26 makes the AI ruling on a no-show final. The chat log's 0.6 weight caps confidence in anything drawn from it alone; it sets no floor below which this trip must go to a human.

If the judge instead finds that whether the driver messaged before cancelling cannot be established at all, POL-GEN-26 makes the outcome ESCALATE with that open question stated — and escalation holds the amount, it does not release it. NO_ACTION would be wrong here: the present state (payment_status REFUNDED, refund_issued_sgd 5.00, the fee already recovered from the driver) leaves the driver 5.00 SGD out of pocket, and POL-GEN-03's NO_ACTION preserves that state rather than restoring the charge.

ruling.explanation:
The events up to the wait are not in dispute and the record confirms them. The driver arrived at the pickup at 11:11:50 — the trip record's arrival event is corroborated by the GPS trace, whose nearest fix sits 2.05 m from the pickup with 5 m reported accuracy, inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius (POL-NS-21). The 300-second free wait therefore ran from 11:11:50 to 11:16:50, and the driver cancelled at 11:18:10, 380 seconds after arrival. That much of the driver's case is accepted: the wait was served and the fee is not void for want of waiting.

The case turns on the driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23, which requires BOTH an in-app chat message AND an in-app call before cancelling. The call limb is met on clean evidence: one in-app call at 11:14:20, unanswered after 20 s, before the 11:18:10 cancellation (EV-TRIP-05065). The message limb cannot be decided either way. The chat export (EV-CHAT-05065) is impaired — TRUNCATED_LOG, weight 0.6 — holding only 1 of the 3 messages the trip record counts (chat_message_count 3), with nothing after 11:06:00, so the arrival and the entire waiting window are absent. That is exactly the stretch where a driver's pre-cancellation message would sit. An impaired limb is undecided, and POL-GEN-26 names this very fact — 'whether the driver messaged and called before cancelling' — as one that, where the evidence carrying it is missing or impaired, escalates the case instead of deciding it; POL-NS-26 subjects even the final no-show ruling to POL-GEN-26.

So the driver's request to have the 5.00 SGD restored (POL-NS-22: DRIVER_COMPENSATION, both amount fields 5.00) is rejected — it needs the message limb to hold, and an undecided limb cannot support restoring the fee. The driver is right that a truncated export does not prove a message was never sent, but it does not prove one was sent either, so that point does not carry the fee. The rider's contrary argument — that the fee is voided because the message limb is missing — goes equally too far: the message is unproven, not proven absent, so POL-NS-23's FULL_REFUND trigger is not established and the rider cannot be declared the winner on it. The rider's submission that the present state should simply stand as NO_ACTION under POL-GEN-03 is rejected too: escalation holds the amount rather than leaving a money outcome in place.

Confidence is capped at 0.6, the weight of the impaired chat log that carries the undecided fact (POL-GEN-02(2)); the required bar here is POL-NS-26's, and the 5.00 SGD disputed value sits below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band with fraud_flags 0 on both profiles, so no higher bar applies. No referral is produced: the rider profile carries no no_show_cancellations_30d counter, so POL-NS-25's repeat no-show flag cannot be computed, and the 5.00 SGD charged matches the 5.00 SGD policy fee, so POL-NS-22's fee-amount referral does not fire. The open question for the human reviewer is whether the driver sent an in-app chat message before cancelling; the 5.00 SGD already refunded to the rider and withheld from the driver is held as it stands, neither collected nor refunded further, pending that review.

What is not in doubt: the driver arrived. The trip record's driver_arrived event at 11:11:50 is corroborated by the GPS trace, whose nearest fix sits 2.05 m from the pickup with 5 m reported accuracy, well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius of POL-NS-21. The driver cancelled at 11:18:10, 380 s after arrival, past the 300 s free wait POL-NS-21 requires. The call limb of POL-NS-23 is also met — one in-app call at 11:14:20, before the cancellation.

What cannot be established is the other half of POL-NS-23's contact obligation: that the driver sent at least one in-app chat message before cancelling. The only artifact that would carry that fact, the chat log (EV-CHAT-05065), is impaired: TRUNCATED_LOG, weight_multiplier 0.6 — it holds 1 of the trip record's 3 chat messages and nothing after 11:06:00, so the arrival and the entire waiting window are absent from it. POL-GEN-26 names this exact fact ('whether the driver messaged and called before cancelling') as one that escalates when the evidence that would carry it is missing or impaired, and POL-NS-26 expressly subjects a no-show's finality to POL-GEN-26.

Driver: I could not accept that the fee stands. POL-NS-22 gives you compensation only 'where the fee stands', and the fee stands only if POL-NS-23's contact obligation holds; an impaired limb is undecided, and an undecided limb supports neither the payment you seek nor the refund the rider seeks. I could not accept that the rider's statement fills the gap either — POL-NS-23 reads the chat log and the trip record, not a party's recollection. Rider: I could not accept that the message limb 'fails'. The truncated export does not show a message is missing; it shows the message cannot be seen, so the fee is not voided on this record either. Your point that a platform arrival push is not a chat message and an unanswered call is not a message is correct, but it does not put the missing entries back.

No referral is available: the rider profile carries no no_show_cancellations_30d counter, so POL-NS-25's repeat-no-show flag cannot be computed, and the fee is the policy's 5.00 SGD, so POL-NS-22's amount check does not fire. Confidence is 0.6, capped by the impaired chat log, the only artifact carrying the message fact; the dispute value is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band. Open question for the reviewer: did the driver send an in-app chat message before cancelling (the chat entries after 11:06:00 are missing)?

ruling.explanation:
This case turns on the driver's contact obligation, not on his arrival or his wait — those are proved, and I accept them; the obligation's message limb is the one thing the record leaves unresolved, and the policy sends an unresolved fact to a human.

Both parties' evidence agrees on the following, and I accept it. The driver reached the pickup at 11:11:50 (EV-TRIP-05065), and the GPS trace corroborates it: the nearest fix is 2.05 m from the pickup at 11:12:30 with 5 m reported accuracy, inside the 50 m STANDARD radius, and the trace holds thirteen zero-speed fixes at the pickup through 11:18:00 (EV-GPS-05065, weight 1.0). The 300 s free wait (POL-NS-21) ran from 11:11:50 and expired at 11:16:50; the driver cancelled at 11:18:10, 380 s after arrival. POL-NS-21 is discharged and POL-NS-22's precondition — cancellation after the free wait — is met.

POL-NS-23, however, requires the driver to have sent at least one in-app chat message AND placed at least one in-app call before cancelling, and voids the fee if either is missing. The call is on the record: one in-app call at 11:14:20, unanswered (EV-TRIP-05065). The message cannot be tested. The chat log (EV-CHAT-05065) is impaired — issue code TRUNCATED_LOG, weight_multiplier 0.6 — holding 1 entry (the rider's 11:06:00 message) against the trip record's chat_message_count of 3, with nothing after 11:06:00: the arrival and the whole waiting window are absent. The limb reads exactly the stretch the defect covers, so it is undecided. I do not accept the rider's reading that a truncated export proves the message 'is missing' — it proves no such thing — and I do not accept the driver's reading that the limb is therefore met.

An undecided limb supports neither the payment the driver needs it to support (POL-NS-22, DRIVER_COMPENSATION) nor a refund the rider would need it to fail for (POL-NS-23, FULL_REFUND). POL-GEN-26 names this very fact — 'whether the driver messaged and called before cancelling' — and requires escalation with the open question stated, which is the ruling here. ESCALATE is terminal: no money issues, and the 5.00 SGD reversed on 2026-09-08 (fee_reversed at 13:59:10; EV-FARE-05065 shows refund_issued_sgd 5.00 against total_charged 5.00) is held rather than restored to the driver or collected from the rider. NO_ACTION, which the rider also urged, is for a claim the evidence answers against; this evidence does not answer at all.

Confidence: the deciding fact rests on the impaired chat log, EV-CHAT-05065, weight 0.6, issue code TRUNCATED_LOG. The trip record (1.0) records the count that reveals the gap but comes from the same chat store, so it is not an independent carrier and does not lift the cap: confidence 0.6. The bar is 0.0 for a 5.00 SGD no-show with a fraud_flags of 0 on both profiles (POL-GEN-22, POL-NS-26).

Referrals: none arises. POL-NS-22's referral applies only where the amount charged was not 5.00 SGD (it was exactly 5.00); POL-NS-25's applies only where rider_profile carries a no_show_cancellations_30d counter of 3 or more (that counter is absent, and no_show_disputes_30d is a different field, context-only under POL-GEN-01); POL-NS-24's goodwill credit applies only where the driver failed to reach the pickup on time or failed to attempt contact — this was an on-demand trip with no scheduled time, and the driver did call.

Open question for the human reviewer: did the driver send an in-app chat message before cancelling at 11:18:10? The complete chat export, which the rider's own account ('never got any message that he arrived. Only a missed call') does not by itself supply, should settle it.

An undecided limb supports neither the payment the driver needs it to support (POL-NS-22, DRIVER_COMPENSATION) nor a refund the rider would need it to fail for (POL-NS-23, FULL_REFUND). ruling.explanation:
Both parties: the 5.00 SGD no-show fee was charged to the rider on 2026-09-08, then reversed after the rider's complaint and withheld from the driver, and the driver filed to have it restored to him. This record cannot decide the case, so it goes to human review with the open question stated below.

What is settled. The driver arrived: the trip record's 11:11:50 arrival event (EV-TRIP-05065) is corroborated by his GPS trace (EV-GPS-05065), whose nearest fix sits 2.05 m from the pickup with 5 m reported accuracy, inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius. He served the 300 s free wait POL-NS-21 requires: the clock runs from arrival at 11:11:50, expiring 11:16:50, and he cancelled at 11:18:10 — 380 s later. The call limb of POL-NS-23 is met: one in-app call at 11:14:20, unanswered, placed before cancellation (EV-TRIP-05065).

What is not settled. POL-NS-23 also requires the driver to have sent at least one in-app chat message before cancelling. The chat log (EV-CHAT-05065) is impaired — TRUNCATED_LOG, weight 0.6 — holding 1 of the 3 messages the trip record counts, with nothing after 11:06:00, so the arrival and the whole waiting window are absent. That is exactly the stretch that limb reads. An impaired limb is undecided, not disproved: the fee is neither voided on POL-NS-23 nor upheld on POL-NS-22. POL-GEN-26 names this very fact — 'whether the driver messaged and called before cancelling' — and requires escalation. POL-NS-26 makes an AI no-show ruling final but expressly subjects it to POL-GEN-26. The 5.00 SGD already refunded to the rider and withheld from the driver is therefore held, not collected and not further moved, pending the reviewer's finding on that open question.

Rejected. The rider's argument that the fee is voided because the record shows no driver message fails: the truncation leaves the message unproved, not disproved. The driver's argument that the 5.00 must be paid to him fails for the mirror reason: his contact obligation is not shown to be met. The rider's argument for NO_ACTION fails because it needs the message limb to have failed, which it has not.

No referral fires. The fee is exactly the 5.00 SGD policy figure, so POL-NS-22's fee-amount referral does not apply and its DRIVER_COMPENSATION direction is not reached; POL-NS-24's goodwill credit does not apply, the driver having attempted contact by call; and the rider's profile carries no no_show_cancellations_30d counter (EV-RPROF-05065), so POL-NS-25's repeat no-show flag cannot be computed.

Confidence 0.6, capped by the impaired chat log (weight 0.6, TRUNCATED_LOG) that carries the undecidable fact.

ledger.claim: POL-NS-23 requires the driver, before cancelling for no-show, to have sent at least one in-app chat message AND to have placed at least one in-app call, both before trip_record.cancelled_at. The record shows the call limb only — a single in-app call at 11:14:20 that was not answered and rang 20 s (EV-TRIP-05065) — and no chat message from the driver at all: the chat log's one and only entry is the rider's own message at 11:06:00, and the platform's own derived contact_before_cancel block returns message_count 0, complete false and obligation_met false (EV-CHAT-05065). I rely on EV-CHAT-05065 as impaired evidence: TRUNCATED_LOG, weight_multiplier 0.6, 1 of 3 entries exported with nothing after 11:06:00. On the record as it stands the message limb of the contact obligation fails, and POL-NS-23 is express that the fee is then voided 'with no driver compensation' — so the driver cannot recover the 5.00 under POL-NS-22 even though he cancelled 380 s after arriving.

The driver's claim says he 'sent message and called', but the trip record's own event log shows what actually happened at that pickup: a platform push notification at 11:11:54 ('Your driver has arrived') and one in-app call at 11:14:20 that was not answered (EV-TRIP-05065). A system push is not an in-app chat message, and an unanswered call is not a message; POL-NS-23 requires both limbs, each before the cancellation, and nothing in this record supplies the message limb. The chat log I rely on for that is impaired — TRUNCATED_LOG, weight_multiplier 0.6 (EV-CHAT-05065).

If the judge reads the truncated chat export as leaving the message limb unproved rather than disproved, the rider still wins the money point: whether the driver messaged before cancelling is a fact POL-NS-23 needs, and the only evidence that would carry it is impaired — the export holds 1 entry against trip_record.chat_message_count of 3 and covers nothing after 11:06:00, so the arrival and the whole waiting window are absent (EV-CHAT-05065, weight_multiplier 0.6, TRUNCATED_LOG; EV-TRIP-05065). POL-GEN-26 names this very fact ('whether the driver messaged and called before cancelling') and requires escalation. ESCALATE is terminal, issues no monetary outcome and holds the amount, so the 5.00 already refunded to the rider is not restored to the driver and no fee is collected from the rider. POL-NS-26 expressly subjects even a final no-show ruling to POL-GEN-26.

I do not contest the wait, and I say so plainly: POL-NS-21's free wait runs 300 s from the driver's arrival, the record puts arrival at 11:11:50 and cancellation at 11:18:10 — 380 s — and the GPS trace corroborates the arrival, the nearest fix sitting 2.05 m from the pickup at 11:12:30 with 5.0 m reported accuracy, well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius (EV-GPS-05065; EV-TRIP-05065). That discharges POL-NS-21 and it does nothing for POL-NS-23, which is a separate and cumulative contact obligation the driver must also satisfy before he may cancel for no-show.

The filer here is the driver (dispute.filed_by = DRIVER) and the disputed 5.00 is already off the rider: the ledger records payment_status REFUNDED with refund_issued_sgd 5.00 against total_charged 5.00 (EV-FARE-05065), and the trip record records the fee_reversed event at 13:59:10 — 5.00 refunded to the rider and withheld from the driver (EV-TRIP-05065). What the driver seeks is restoration of that 5.00 to himself. POL-GEN-03 defines FULL_REFUND against the filing party, so on a driver's filing FULL_REFUND would run to the driver; it is not the rider's remedy and the rider does not ask for it. The rider's entitlement is that the disputed charge is not collected, which is exactly what the present state already achieves: NO_ACTION — the filing party's claim not supported, both amount fields null and no driver compensation.

No POL-NS-25 repeat-no-show referral is available on this profile. EV-RPROF-05065 carries no no_show_cancellations_30d counter at all, and POL-NS-25 applies only where that counter is present, so the flag cannot be computed and must not be manufactured from the record. The profile's no_show_disputes_30d is a different field, is CONTEXT ONLY under POL-GEN-01, and may not be used to qualify or decide this trip.

ledger.claim: The driver's arrival at the pickup is established on clean evidence: the trip record's driver_arrived event at 11:11:50 is corroborated by the driver's GPS trace under POL-NS-21, whose nearest fix to the pickup point is 2.05 m away with a reported accuracy of 5 m — well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius — and the arrival check returns corroborated true.

The driver served the free wait in fact, not merely on paper: the driver's trace carries thirteen consecutive zero-speed fixes holding position at the pickup from 11:11:30 through 11:18:00, and the platform recorded wait_timer_expired at 11:16:55 with the rider not on board, so the 300 s POL-NS-21 requires was actually waited.

The cancellation came after the free wait: POL-NS-21's clock starts from the driver's arrival (11:11:50) so the 300 s free wait expired at 11:16:50, while the driver cancelled at 11:18:10 — 380 s after arrival — which satisfies POL-NS-22's precondition of a cancellation after the free wait.

The call limb of POL-NS-23 is satisfied on the clean record: the trip record's in_app_calls carries one call placed by the driver at 11:14:20, unanswered after ringing 20 s, which is before cancelled_at (11:18:10) and is exactly the trip_record.in_app_calls entry the clause names.

The message limb is not shown to be missing. The chat log is IMPAIRED — issue code TRUNCATED_LOG, weight multiplier 0.6 — because the export holds only 1 entry (11:06:00) while trip_record.chat_message_count is 3, and the absent entries cover the arrival and the entire waiting window. POL-NS-23 voids the fee only where the driver's message 'is missing', and the absence of a message from a truncated export does not establish that no message was ever sent.

The counterparty statement does not fill that gap: the rider concedes the call ('Only a missed call') and asserts only that he received no arrival message, and a party's recollection of what he did or did not receive cannot establish what the platform's own chat system carried before the cancellation.

With the arrival, the free wait and the call all carried by artifacts at weight 1.0, the fee is not voided and the ledger's own arithmetic compels the driver's outcome: the fare breakdown charges 5.00 SGD, the policy fee is 5.00 SGD, fee_matches_policy is true, so POL-NS-22 directs DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 5.00.

No confidence floor bars that ruling: the amount contested is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and the only profile field POL-GEN-22 makes relevant is fraud_flags, which is 0 on both profiles, so neither the 0.80 nor the 0.95 threshold applies, and POL-NS-26 makes the AI ruling on a no-show final. The chat log's 0.6 weight caps confidence in anything drawn from it alone; it sets no floor below which this trip must go to a human.

If the judge instead finds that whether the driver messaged before cancelling cannot be established at all, POL-GEN-26 makes the outcome ESCALATE with that open question stated — and escalation holds the amount, it does not release it. NO_ACTION would be wrong here: the present state (payment_status REFUNDED, refund_issued_sgd 5.00, the fee already recovered from the driver) leaves the driver 5.00 SGD out of pocket, and POL-GEN-03's NO_ACTION preserves that state rather than restoring the charge.
